tools.description: [read] Explains Log Commander for an AI: concepts (tab, view, entry, epoch), the filter tree with examples, the SQL table of the dashboard, field rules, recipes for common questions, limits and error codes. Call it once before a larger task. Works even when the app is closed.

topic.description: Omit for the overview and the list of topics

tools.name: help

tools.description: [read] The open tabs: id, title (a filter tab shows its chain 'app.log › ERROR'), kind (file, merge, source), path or source label, profile, lines in the file and in the view, frozen, following, status, and which tab is in front. Start here. Tabs the user hid from AI are not listed.
tools.name: get_workspace

tools.description: [read] One tab in detail: everything of get_workspace plus its filter (levels, search, filter tree), its columns (ids for field conditions, fields and SQL), the selected entry, bookmarks and notes, epoch and view_generation, and whether a filter job is still running.

tab_id.description: Tab id from get_workspace; default: the tab in front

tools.name: get_tab

tools.description: [read] Counts per level for the whole file and for the view of the tab, file size, number of entries and the time span of the file. Cheap: use it before reading any lines.

tab_id.description: Tab id from get_workspace; default: the tab in front

tools.name: get_stats

tools.description: [read] Lines of the tab's view (filtered as the user sees it), each with line (file, 1-based), pos (position in the view, 1-based), level, continuation (part of a stack trace) and text. Give start (view position; negative counts from the end: -50 = the last 50) or around_line (a file line; the window is centred on it). fields: true adds the columns split ({column id: value}). Never page through a whole log: locate first with get_stats, find_level, search, get_timeline or run_sql.

around_line.description: Line number of the file, 1-based (as the gutter shows it)

epoch.description: The epoch of an earlier answer: fails with stale_view if the file was truncated, rotated without keeping or re-sorted since, so line numbers you hold no longer fit

fields.description: Add the split columns per line

start.description: View position, 1-based; negative: from the end (-1 = last line). Default -count

tab_id.description: Tab id from get_workspace; default: the tab in front

tools.name: read_lines

tools.description: [read] The whole entry of a line: its head and all continuation lines (stack trace, wrapped JSON), straight from the file, ignoring the filter. Use it to read an exception completely.

epoch.description: The epoch of an earlier answer: fails with stale_view if the file was truncated, rotated without keeping or re-sorted since, so line numbers you hold no longer fit

line.description: Line number of the file, 1-based (as the gutter shows it)

tab_id.description: Tab id from get_workspace; default: the tab in front

tools.name: get_entry

tools.description: [read] Finds lines in the tab's view containing query (text or regex), from from_line on (default the start; backwards: from the end), stops after limit hits or when it wraps around. Returns line, pos and the line text. Does not change the search of the tab – to show the result to the user use open_filter_tab.

epoch.description: The epoch of an earlier answer: fails with stale_view if the file was truncated, rotated without keeping or re-sorted since, so line numbers you hold no longer fit

from_line.description: Line number of the file, 1-based (as the gutter shows it)

tab_id.description: Tab id from get_workspace; default: the tab in front

tools.name: search

tools.description: [read] Heads of the next entries with one of levels (default ERROR and FATAL) in the tab's view, from from_line on (default the start; backwards: from the end). Fast (uses the level index, no text scan): the best way to list errors. Follow up with get_entry for the stack trace.

epoch.description: The epoch of an earlier answer: fails with stale_view if the file was truncated, rotated without keeping or re-sorted since, so line numbers you hold no longer fit

from_line.description: Line number of the file, 1-based (as the gutter shows it)

tab_id.description: Tab id from get_workspace; default: the tab in front

tools.name: find_level

tools.description: [read] Entries of the whole file over time: buckets with counts of all entries, WARN, ERROR and FATAL, plus gaps (stretches without any entry – outages, a stopped service). Without from/to the axis spans the 1st to 99th percentile of the times. Counts are approximate. Use it for 'when did it start' and 'was there an outage'.

tab_id.description: Tab id from get_workspace; default: the tab in front

tools.name: get_timeline

tools.description: [read] The first entry at or after a time in the tab's view: its line and pos. Then read_lines around_line to see what happened.

tab_id.description: Tab id from get_workspace; default: the tab in front

tools.name: line_at_time

tools.description: [read] The SQL table of the tab for run_sql: columns with type and meaning (line, ts, level, source and the number fields of the format), and whether it is still being built. Builds it on first use.

tab_id.description: Tab id from get_workspace; default: the tab in front

tools.name: report_schema

tools.description: [read] One read-only SQLite query over the entry heads of the tab's file (help topic sql): table log(line, ts ms UTC, level, source, fields…), bucket(ts, '1m') for time series. The best tool for counting, grouping, top-N and percentiles. Never contains the message text. Example: SELECT bucket(ts, '1m') AS t, count(*) AS n FROM log WHERE level = 'ERROR' GROUP BY t ORDER BY t

tab_id.description: Tab id from get_workspace; default: the tab in front

tools.name: run_sql

tools.description: [read] Tries an extraction rule (a regex with exactly one group over a column) on the last lines of the tab's view and returns what it would extract per line. Saves nothing – propose_field_rule asks the user to keep it.

lines.description: How many lines from the end to try

pattern.description: Regex with exactly one capture group, e.g. took (\d+ ?ms)

source_column.description: Column id the regex runs over

tab_id.description: Tab id from get_workspace; default: the tab in front

tools.name: preview_field_rule

tools.description: [read] The actions of the app run_action may run: id, name (German) and group. Only harmless view actions (next error, freeze, column view, …).
tools.name: list_actions

tools.description: [read] Waits for new lines in the tab (live tail) that match query and/or levels, up to timeout_s, and returns the first ones – or timed_out: true. Matching runs in the app (entries with stack traces count as one). Use it for 'tell me when X happens'; call it again to keep watching.

tab_id.description: Tab id from get_workspace; default: the tab in front

tools.description: [changes the view, visible to the user] Replaces the filter of a tab (level chips, search, filter tree). Prefer open_filter_tab: it leaves the user's filter alone. Omitted parts are reset (levels: all, no search, empty tree). Waits up to 30 s for the filter job.

search.description: The search of the tab (toolbar). mode filter: only matching entries; highlight: all lines, matches marked

tab_id.description: Tab id from get_workspace; default: the tab in front

oneOf.description: A column of the tab (get_tab columns). gt/lt/between compare numbers in base units: took > 500ms is value "500ms"
Time of the entry, ISO 8601 (without zone: local time)
Section between a start and an end pattern (e.g. a request from 'begin 42' to 'end 42')
Line numbers of the file, 1-based like everywhere in these tools; first or last may be null (open end)

tree.description: Filter tree (help topic filters): a group with op and/or and children; a condition holds for an entry once one of its lines (head or stack trace) meets it. negate: NOT. At most 64 conditions, 16 levels deep.

tools.name: set_filter

tools.description: [changes the view, visible to the user] Opens a filter tab below a tab: it shows the parent's view AND this filter, live, titled like 'app.log › ERROR'. The preferred way to show a result. At most 8 tabs per file. Example tree for 'errors without health checks': {"kind":"group","op":"and","children":[{"kind":"cond","cond":{"type":"level","levels":["ERROR","FATAL"]}},{"kind":"cond","negate":true,"cond":{"type":"text","text":"/health","isRegex":false,"caseSensitive":false}}]}
